The team’s work covers the full physical planning and development of data center sites, from initial site programming and master planning through the coordinated design of single-building facilities and large-scale, multi-building campuses. This includes establishing the overall layout, building locations and orientations, land utilization, construction and capacity phasing, central plants, site access and circulation, logistics areas, stormwater management, civil works, and provisions for future expansion.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;The Data Center Engineering team creates an integrated design that coordinates each data center building with power, cooling, water, telecommunications, controls, life-safety, security, and other shared infrastructure systems. The team is also responsible for the comprehensive design of the buildings and their supporting systems and equipment, including architecture, structure, building envelope, mechanical systems, electrical infrastructure, plumbing, controls, fire protection, and life-safety systems. The team coordinates the full design lifecycle from early-stage site planning and project definition through detailed design, construction, commissioning support, and IT deployment. It makes sure CoreWeave’s technical requirements are built into each project and delivered in line with established scope, schedule, budget, quality, reliability, scalability, and operational expectations. Through disciplined leadership, multidisciplinary design coordination, and consistent execution, the team enables CoreWeave to rapidly and reliably expand its physical infrastructure to support next-generation, high-density compute workloads.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We are seeking an accomplished and experienced Director of Data Center Engineering to lead CoreWeave’s multidisciplinary team of engineering subject matter experts and set the technical direction for our global data center portfolio. This role will be accountable for the management and coordination of multidisciplinary design activities across Greenfield developments, build-to-suit facilities, leased data centers, tenant fit-outs, renovations, infrastructure upgrades, and equipment replacement projects.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;As a peer to the Director, Data Center Engineering and Director, Data Center Technology, the Director, Design Management will focus on design execution, project governance, resource allocation, consultant performance, and portfolio delivery. You will maintain visibility across both Land and Lease execution paths, ensure deal review timelines align to pipeline commitments, and lead the strategic sequencing of new market entry across multiple active international programs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This role is based in our US hubs and has a global remit, which may require periodic international travel.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h4\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;In this role, you will:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h4\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Define MW market direction by location and develop a demand-to-supply alignment framework, translating capacity requirements into prioritized site specifications across domestic and international markets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own end-to-end program management for CoreWeave\u0026#39;s international data center expansion — coordinate across Legal, Finance, Engineering, and Operations to sequence and deliver new market entry milestones across EMEA, APAC, and emerging markets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Maintain integrated project plans, dependency maps, and risk registers across all active international programs, ensuring continuous leadership visibility into program health and schedule risk.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Coordinate with the Due Diligence Team (managed by VP, Development) to align deal review timelines to intake and pipeline commitments; maintain full demand-to-execution visibility across both Land and Lease paths.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Manage direct report(s) responsible for maintaining the interdependency tracker between the Omni/CWaaS international pipeline and domestic development pipeline, supporting resource alignment and program sequencing.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build and run portfolio reviews, steering committees, and senior stakeholder forums to align on program sequencing, resource needs, and market prioritization decisions.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Develop and maintain standardized intake and pipeline processes across matrixed, fast-moving teams to improve cycle times and decision quality at scale.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h4\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Who You Are\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h4\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;8-12 years in program/operations management, strategy, or deal management within data center, technology infrastructure, or capital-intensive sectors.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Demonstrated experience managing international expansion programs across multiple geographies, including EMEA and APAC markets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Proven ability to build and manage complex multi-workstream pipeline and intake processes across matrixed, fast-moving organizations.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Strong executive presence; This is a highly technical leadership role. We are building security that runs at machine speed: every change threat modeled at design time, reviewed before it merges, and attacked by our own agents before an adversary gets the chance. What our agents find, our agents fix. Threat models arrive in minutes. Pentesting stops being a queue: agents cover the breadth around the clock, third party firms add depth, and our internal team goes after the hardest targets. Humans set policy and make the consequential calls. Security is one of the reasons customers pick CoreWeave, and this org is a big part of how we earn it.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;We are agentic first because the surface is growing faster than any team we could hire, and we expect this leader to build the systems that make that real. You will also set the bar for how security shows up for CoreWeave engineers: a paved road instead of a toll booth, a product they want to use rather than a tax they have to pay.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Key Responsibilities:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Define and drive the strategy and roadmap for Product Security at CoreWeave, spanning application security, vulnerability management, offensive security, AI product security, and product vulnerability response.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Lead and grow a multi-team organization of managers and senior ICs, including hiring the engineering managers who will run each function.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build an agentic-first vulnerability program where agents discover, triage, and remediate issues at scale, with the goal of retiring entire classes of risk rather than closing tickets one at a time.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own vulnerability management end to end across CoreWeave\u0026#39;s infrastructure and products: discovery, prioritization, SLAs, remediation, and reporting to executive leadership.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Run a tiered offensive security program that combines continuous agentic testing, third party assessments, an internal team focused on our hardest targets, and external researchers through our vulnerability disclosure and bug bounty programs. Adversarial testing of our models, agents, and inference stack is part of the job, built for how AI fails: prompt injection, poisoned tools, and abuse of autonomy.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Bring offensive security to bear on tenant isolation across shared GPUs, bare metal, and Kubernetes. Platform Security owns the isolation controls and strategy; Product Security makes sure they hold.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build the paved road for CoreWeave engineers: secure defaults, controls built into the tools engineers already use, and findings that arrive validated with the fix attached.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Establish one secure development It provides access control, protected aliases, lineage, and automation hooks, and it is where a model version goes once it moves out of research. Pinterest, Capital One, Canva, Recursion, and Dropbox all run on it, and for some of them it sits inside a production serving path. Artifacts is the layer underneath it: content-addressable storage, deduplication, lineage, and retention for datasets, model weights, checkpoints, and evaluation outputs, across S3, GCS, Azure, and CoreWeave AI Object Storage. Every object logged to W\u0026amp;amp;B is an artifact.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;The team\u0026#39;s mandate is also weighted heavily toward closing the gap between CoreWeave\u0026#39;s infrastructure and the ML experimentation that happens in W\u0026amp;amp;B. That includes extending the Registry beyond a record of decisions, so that promoting a model version can put it into serving on CoreWeave compute with lineage and access control carried through, and bringing compute and experimentation into a single unified experience rather than separate tools. This work is done in partnership with foundational infrastructure teams at CoreWeave and product teams across the W\u0026amp;amp;B ecosystem.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;The current scope is well defined and load bearing, with enterprise customers relying on it daily. What is open is what comes next, where there is significant room for new products, new roadmaps, and deeper integration between CoreWeave and W\u0026amp;amp;B. The role therefore calls for a product-first mindset alongside strong operational ownership.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the role\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You\u0026#39;ll own the full lifecycle, from roadmap shaping through delivery and production reliability. Operating in a high-stakes, 24/7 setting, this team is responsible for safeguarding the availability, stability, and reliability of mission-critical systems that power our most essential services.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;As a Facilities Command Center Engineer, you bring facilities engineering judgment to mission control for our global data center fleet. Where a site engineer owns one building, you see every building at once. You will conduct structured remote rounds across every site we operate using BMS, EPMS, DCIM, and every other telemetry source available to us, and when something looks wrong, you are the person who works out what it means.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Our telemetry is not always timely or clean, and not every alarm has a runbook. This role exists for those moments. You will read one-line diagrams and sequences of operation, diagnose electrical, mechanical, and fire protection events from incomplete data, decide whether and where to send people, and make sure work in the field is safe and authorized before it starts.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;This is a remote engineering role performed from the Command Center. You will not be turning wrenches, but you need to understand the equipment as if you had, because the person turning the wrench is relying on your call.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Key responsibilities:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Diagnose moderate-to-high complexity issues across electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety systems using telemetry, one-line diagrams, P\u0026amp;amp;IDs, sequences of operation, and equipment documentation.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Make the call when no runbook fits: assess risk to production, decide whether to dispatch, and direct the first response within defined limits.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Review work requests, MOPs, and change records submitted by site teams and vendors for safety and operational compliance before work is authorized.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Conduct scheduled remote rounds each shift, reviewing and recording the health of electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety systems across the fleet.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Monitor critical assets including UPS systems, standby generators and fuel systems, switchgear, PDUs, battery plant, chillers, CRAH/CRAC units, cooling towers, pumps, air handlers, and fire suppression systems.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Baseline normal operating conditions, trend performance across sites, and identify drift and early-warning signatures before they become events.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Serve as first responder for infrastructure alarms, triaging incidents and initiating response per SOPs, MOPs, and EOPs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Escalate to on-site operations, engineering teams, and leadership based on defined escalation matrices, with a clear technical assessment attached.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Coordinate incident response across multiple teams and sites, and remotely support on-site technicians, vendors, and contractors during events and planned maintenance.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Write and correct operating procedures based on what you see across the fleet, and feed lessons learned back to site leadership.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Act as technical lead on root cause analysis, providing timelines, alarm histories, and an engineering read of what failed and why.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Coach Command Center Technicians on your crew and help them build the facilities depth to grow into this role.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Maintain detailed event logs and lead structured shift handovers to keep operations continuous across crews.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Work Schedule:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;Our Command Center operates 24/7/365. You will be assigned to a night crew,\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Shift: 12.5 hours, including a 30-minute handover overlap at each end of the shift.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Rotation: A fixed two-week repeating pattern (2-2-3) with every other weekend off. Its charter is to make sure operations engineers have access to information that is easily digestible, non-repetitive, indexable, and aligned with other engineering teams. Its corpus includes the FROps onboarding curriculum, the Site Bring-up Playbook, the FROps Systems Web, the Engineering Teams and escalation reference, Region Quirks, the FROps Vocabulary, and the runbooks operations engineers follow when standing up and remediating nodes.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This role sits within Knowledge Architecture and works day-to-day with FRO-OED as its primary stakeholder. So far, we’ve:\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Released \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://github.com/openpipe/art\u0026quot;\u0026gt;ART\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, the easiest library for getting started with RL.\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Developed \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44535078\u0026quot;\u0026gt;RULER,\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt; a general-purpose reward function that works across many diverse tasks.\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Built \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://wandb.ai/site/serverless-rl/\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Serverless RL\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt;, an elegant API that gives RL practitioners full control over their data, environment, and reward function while letting them outsource the headaches of managing GPU infrastructure.\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;These releases have a theme: we’re systematically tackling each major roadblock to successfully training self-improving agents. Several serious challenges remain. Building simulated environments often requires substantial human labor, and existing training methods are not data-efficient enough. We\u0026#39;re laser-focused on solving these problems and making self-improvement a reality for agent developers.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;In startup terms, this is a classic hard-tech bet. Our roadmap involves substantial\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt; technical risk;\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; there are still major technical problems we’re facing without a proven solution. However, there is very little \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;market risk.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; We’ve worked closely with the teams building agents at many of the top AI-native startups as well as large enterprises. \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;If we can build this, everyone will want it.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; A self improving agent that learns from experience the way a human employee would could quickly capture a large fraction of the total inference market, which is worth tens of billions of dollars today and will be worth hundreds of billions in a few years.\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the Role\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You have trained LLMs to be SOTA on specific tasks. You have opinions on whether sequence-level or token-level importance ratios are more effective. You probably shared the \u0026lt;a href=\u0026quot;https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13786\u0026quot;\u0026gt;ScaleRL\u0026lt;/a\u0026gt; paper in your group chats, and kicked off a few ablations after you read it.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You will be expected to generate and investigate research ideas towards solving the remaining obstacles to \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;continuous learning in production\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;. You will work with the broader CRAFT team to validate these research directions across real customer tasks. We are very GPU rich and are ready to direct an enormous amount of compute at this effort.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Beyond your role’s specific qualifications, we’re looking for strong engineers with great taste. The most important qualification by far is that you \u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;learn fast\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt; and can ship. This role will inevitably involve a lot of learning on the job; we’re building this airplane as we fly it. Engineers on our team touch everything from CUDA kernels to high-performance LLM tracing dashboards, and you will have an opportunity to touch many parts of this stack. Although we operate as part of a larger company, the CRAFT team is small, has a large degree of autonomy and drives our own roadmap and priorities. This is an excellent role for someone looking to find their own company in the future.\u0026amp;nbsp;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Required CoreWeave is a dynamic, high-growth technology company, and for this role we especially want someone who independently tackles ambiguous, complex capacity questions and improves how the team solves them.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;As a Senior Network Capacity Planner, you will make sure our global data center network infrastructure is optimized for scalability and efficiency. This role requires deep technical fluency in network design topologies and capacity planning and forecasting models, plus the judgment to balance risk, data, and business priorities in your recommendations.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Key Responsibilities:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own capacity forecasting models for network infrastructure across backbone, metro, data center, and edge networks. Flag design trade-offs before they become capacity constraints.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own network hardware and optical component forecasting (e.g., switches, routers, optics, transceivers) end-to-end. Anticipate how priorities and lead times will change, align with Finance and Supply Chain Procurement, and adjust supply planning and procurement recommendations to match.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own bandwidth, port, and optical transport capacity forecasts based on customer growth, product expansion, and usage patterns, weighing competing signals and evidence to make high-confidence recommendations.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Independently analyze network utilization trends, identify systemic bottlenecks or inefficiencies, and drive the resulting optimization work to completion.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Lead scenario and what-if analysis for high-stakes decisions on network expansions and build-outs, and present clear recommendations to stakeholders and leadership.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Collaborate with data center, compute, and GPU planning teams to keep infrastructure capacity aligned across the board, helping teams reach agreement when priorities conflict.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own the process for gathering forward-looking requirements and lead-time visibility from Supply Chain teams, and refine it as the team and portfolio scale.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own KPIs and dashboards that track network hardware forecast accuracy and network capacity. It is organized around what research and platform teams are actually trying to accomplish at this stage, and the infrastructure decisions that either let them move fast or slow them down. SUNK is the most differentiated expression of CoreWeave\u0026#39;s answer to that problem, the product in this scope with the deepest operational proof at scale. The broader story spans CoreWeave Kubernetes Service and a growing Kubernetes-native training surface expanding independently of Slurm. That includes understanding where open source frameworks like Ray, SkyPilot, and Kueue fit in the conversation, where community debate is shaping buyer expectations, and how ecosystem partnerships factor into how teams evaluate and adopt training infrastructure.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You are not inheriting four separate product stories and stitching them together. You are building the connective narrative across CoreWeave\u0026#39;s training stack and the broader ML ecosystem it connects to, including the experiment tracking workflows, open source tooling, and practitioner communities that researchers already operate in. CoreWeave\u0026#39;s integration with Weights and Biases connects infrastructure signals to the experiment tracking tools researchers already use. Part of this role is understanding how that integration shapes researcher perception of CoreWeave and building messaging around it. That means translating capabilities across the stack, topology-aware scheduling, bare-metal performance, Kubernetes-native lifecycle management, automated cluster health management, into messaging that resonates with AI research leaders, platform teams, and the wider ML researcher community beyond the largest labs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h3\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the role:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h3\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;em\u0026gt;Positioning and messaging\u0026lt;/em\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own the AI Training Infrastructure narrative for CoreWeave. That narrative is built on real credibility: CoreWeave infrastructure has been used to train many of the most widely used models in production today. Your job is to deepen and expand that story, building the strategic positioning framework that ties CoreWeave Kubernetes Service, SUNK, and SUNK Anywhere into a coherent market story, deciding how each product is positioned relative to the others, and ensuring that framework holds across every customer-facing surface.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Shape how CoreWeave competes in training-focused sales situations. That means owning the competitive positioning framework field teams use against alternative infrastructure approaches, the persona-specific messaging that translates infrastructure capabilities into outcomes research leaders and platform teams care about, and the launch narrative for new capabilities as they reach the market.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;em\u0026gt;Customer proof\u0026lt;/em\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own the customer evidence strategy for AI Training Infrastructure. Decide which proof points matter for which buyers at which stage. Build the feedback loops that surface deployment insight from Solutions Architects and customer-facing engineers. Ensure that evidence reaches assets without losing specificity in translation. The goal is a proof strategy that makes every customer-facing asset more credible, not a library of case studies.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;em\u0026gt;GTM and sales enablement\u0026lt;/em\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Define how CoreWeave\u0026#39;s training stack goes to market. Own the enablement framework for Sales and Solutions Architects. Set the competitive positioning strategy the field uses in training-focused deals. Partner with DevRel on content and enablement for technical audiences, including developers, researchers, and community contributors. That boundary requires active coordination and will evolve as both roles do. Partner with CoreWeave\u0026#39;s technical and applied ML teams on benchmarking and performance validation that supports how the training stack is positioned and evaluated in market.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;em\u0026gt;Metrics and measurement\u0026lt;/em\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Define how product marketing\u0026#39;s impact is measured for AI Training Infrastructure, not just whether assets were delivered. You will own how we detect, diagnose, and surface performance signals across every data center in our global infrastructure, turning billions of raw telemetry events into real-time insight that engineers, product teams, and executives can act on with confidence.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This is not a straightforward data engineering or BI role. The role will focus on building the observability and insight tooling that lets us answer, in near real time, whether a GPU fleet, a fabric, or a training run is performing the way it should, and why it isn\u0026#39;t when it\u0026#39;s not. If you\u0026#39;re energized by building the systems that turn raw infrastructure telemetry into trusted, actionable performance intelligence, and you want that work to sit closer to the hardware and the workload than to a dashboard, this role was built for you.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;What you\u0026#39;ll do\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Performance Insights \u0026amp;amp; Observability - Design and build the systems that continuously assess AI infrastructure health and performance: GPU utilization and efficiency, interconnect (NVLink, InfiniBand, RoCE) fabric behavior, distributed training and inference throughput, and hardware degradation signals. Build the detection and diagnosis logic that surfaces anomalies and regressions before they become incidents, not just dashboards that report on them after the fact.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Time-Series \u0026amp;amp; Metrics Infrastructure - Own and extend our time-series database (TSDB) layer as the backbone of real-time observability. Write and optimize PromQL/MetricsQL queries that power alerting, anomaly detection, and trend analysis across thousands of GPUs and hundreds of benchmark runs. Bridge streaming metrics and batch-analytical workloads so engineers get sub-second answers during live incidents and analysts get complete historical context for root cause work.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Fabric \u0026amp;amp; GPU Telemetry - Build and validate the pipelines and metrics that make network fabric and GPU-level behavior observable and comparable across racks, clusters, and hardware generations, including gray failure detection, congestion and error-rate signals, and health scoring that holds up under audit.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Data Lake Architecture (in support of insight work) - Design and build the performance data lake that underpins the above: table formats (Apache Iceberg, Parquet, Avro), hot/cold tiering, and schema evolution for latency distributions, throughput metrics, GPU utilization, cost-per-token, and hardware health signals. This is foundational infrastructure, not the end product.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Query Optimization \u0026amp;amp; Performance - Profile and tune query engines against columnar and time-series stores so that the observability layer meets its own strict P99 latency and freshness SLAs. Benchmark the benchmarking infrastructure itself.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;BI \u0026amp;amp; Reporting (secondary) - Where needed, build self-service views (Grafana, Looker, or similar) for engineers, product managers, and executives, but as a downstream output of the insight and observability work above, not the primary deliverable.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Who you are\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;5+ years of experience building distributed systems, observability platforms, or performance engineering tooling, ideally for infrastructure or ML systems rather than general-purpose BI.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Strong coding in Python or Go (C++ a plus) and deep familiarity with networked systems, GPU infrastructure, and performance analysis.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Hands-on experience with Kubernetes at production scale, CI/CD, and observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) used to monitor and diagnose infrastructure, not just report on it.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Working knowledge of time-series databases and fluency in PromQL or MetricsQL for building real-time alerting and anomaly detection, not only historical dashboards.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Familiarity with data lake architectures and modern table formats (Iceberg, Parquet, Avro) sufficient to support an insights platform, though this is not the primary skill this role is hiring for.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Comfortable working close to hardware and workload behavior: GPU utilization patterns, interconnect fabric health, distributed training/inference performance characteristics.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Strong communicator comfortable collaborating with cross-functional teams and external CoreWeave imports and deploys GPUs, servers, networking equipment, UPS units, batteries, and data center infrastructure globally, and is expanding into new regions. That footprint triggers a range of product and environmental obligations, including Extended Producer Responsibility (WEEE, battery, and packaging), RoHS, and REACH. Today those obligations are met through a mix of outside counsel, a Producer Responsibility Organization (PRO), and an advisory engagement to design the operating model. Your job is to bring them together into one program that CoreWeave owns and runs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;You will sit on the Supply Chain Risk/Resilience, Compliance, and Sustainability team, the central control point for compliance across the supply chain. Legal and outside counsel determine what the regulations require. You determine which suppliers and products must do what, collect the data and evidence, submit it to PROs and authorities, and keep the program current as we expand. You will build processes, mature them, hand off steady-state operations to the functional teams, and move on to the next gap.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who has built a product compliance program before and wants to do it again at CoreWeave’s pace, with high visibility into how our GPU and data center supply chain actually runs.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Key Responsibilities:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own CoreWeave’s product compliance program end to end for the hardware we import and deploy. without reinventing the framework underneath them.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Some of what you\u0026#39;ll work on:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own and extend the test framework — that pins to a real host, boots the configuration under test, runs a containerized check, validates it, and records a structured result.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Broaden what the framework qualifies: HPC and fabric verification, Slurm-on-Kubernetes (SUNK), and further down the stack into firmware and hardware, building the abstractions that make new coverage easy to add.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Keep the pipeline fast, hermetic, and trustworthy — boot consistency, per-host resource locking, and ruthless flaky-test elimination — so engineers trust the signal.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own the results and reporting path end to end: structured test results, storage, dashboards, and the triage surfaces engineers use to turn a red run into a root cause quickly.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Explore AI-native testing — LLM-driven log triage, failure classification, and regression detection — as the fleet and test surface grow.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Collaborate with firmware, kernel, imaging, and HPC teams to embed testing into their release process.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Who You Are:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;3+ years of experience building test infrastructure, systems software, or platform tooling at scale, with real ownership of frameworks or automation for low-level software.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Fluent in Python, with either proven Rust experience or a strong systems background (Go, C, C++) and a genuine appetite to build in Rust — the framework\u0026#39;s core is Rust, and you\u0026#39;ll live in it.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Comfortable operating in a Kubernetes environment and reasoning about how software is built, containerized, deployed, and tested.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Solid Linux systems background — the boot chain, kernel and drivers, low-level debugging — and comfort working As the initial engineering representative in the site selection and due diligence process, this individual brings a broad, multidisciplinary perspective to determine how well a site can support CoreWeave’s requirements across all major design disciplines.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the role:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This role serves as the technical bridge between the Site Selection team and the broader Design \u0026amp;amp; Engineering organization. The engineer evaluates infrastructure capacity, utility availability, building suitability, land-use and entitlement considerations, and early design constraints that may affect viability, schedule, or cost. They work directly with data center providers, utilities, landlords, and external partners to clarify technical offerings, identify gaps or risks, and shape early concept direction.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;From initial site introduction through lease execution or acquisition, the Site Selection Design Engineer leads the technical due diligence process - tracking progress, coordinating early design discussions, and ensuring CoreWeave’s requirements are understood from day one. Once a site is secured, the role delivers a structured, thorough handoff to the assigned Design Manager to support a smooth transition into full project design and execution.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;This position demands strong engineering judgment, the ability to interpret information across multiple disciplines, and the confidence to represent CoreWeave’s technical priorities in early strategic conversations.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Frequent travel to prospective data center locations is required.\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;In this role, you will:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Act as the initial technical evaluator for prospective data center sites across electrical, mechanical, architectural, civil, and IT/LV considerations.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Support site evaluation and feasibility efforts by identifying technical risks, constraints, opportunities, and required upgrades.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Serve as the design team leads from initial site concept through lease execution/acquisition, coordinating all design-related activities during these early phases.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Review provider proposals, capacity offers, utility information, conceptual layouts, and as-built drawings to determine alignment with CoreWeave’s design principles.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Interface directly with landlords, developers, data center providers, and utilities during early due diligence.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Prepare concise technical assessments and early go/no-go recommendations to guide which sites advance to deeper analysis.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Prepare and manage dashboards or equivalent tools to track technical progress, risks, land-use considerations, and milestones for all active candidate sites.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Evaluate land use, zoning, permitting, and entitlement feasibility at a high level, identifying potential regulatory constraints or municipal approval risks that may impact schedule, density, or constructability.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Collaborate with internal SMEs and the broader design team as required—resolving early-stage questions independently where possible and escalating discipline-specific topics efficiently to the right experts.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Participate in early design and scoping discussions to establish alignment on CoreWeave requirements and technical expectations.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Review site infrastructure capabilities, including power availability, redundancy options, upstream utility constraints, delivery timelines, and required upgrades.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Assess mechanical feasibility, including heat rejection options, water availability/quality, mechanical yard capacity, and compatibility with CoreWeave cooling strategies (e.g., chilled water plants, CDUs, TCS loops).\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Evaluate building suitability, including structural capacity, floor loading, egress paths, ceiling heights, roof strength, envelope condition, and potential for expansion.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Develop high-level conceptual MEP assessments and identify site blockers that could impact constructability, density, schedule, or cost.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Identify and document site-specific technical risks, delineating clear potential impacts to scope, schedule, and long-term scalability.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Produce technical due diligence summaries that communicate feasibility findings, required upgrades, regulatory considerations, and alignment with CoreWeave’s broader design and operational requirements.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Engage in early technical workshops with providers to ensure proper interpretation of CoreWeave design expectations and project objectives.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Ensure technical requirements are correctly reflected in early documentation such as LOIs, provider proposals, and preliminary agreements.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Perform a structured technical handover to the assigned Design Manager for each site once a lease is executed or the site is acquired, ensuring seamless continuity into full project design.\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;br\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Who You The scope spans asset capacity planning, inbound hardware visibility, receiving, deployment readiness, and lifecycle tracking. You will design and maintain integrations between upstream Supply Chain systems and downstream Data Center platforms, ensuring an accurate, real-time representation of infrastructure assets. As our roadmap expands into data center topology and graph capabilities, this role bridges IT and OT environments, turning raw operational data into reliable, production-grade platforms. Data center capacity is only as valuable as the connectivity that reaches it, and fiber has the longest and least forgiving lead time of any dependency in the expansion pipeline — dark fiber and IRU negotiations, carrier and subsea capacity procurement, permitting and right-of-way, conduit and duct builds, landing station and cable landing point coordination, metro rings, and cross-connects at interconnection facilities. Partner with Legal, Finance, and Sourcing to move agreements through negotiation and execution on the program timeline.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Ensure all active opportunities and programs progress through required intake, review, and approval gates on schedule — flag deviations, at-risk milestones, and sequencing conflicts before they become delays.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Maintain a connectivity view of the portfolio: fiber route inventory, contracted vs. lit capacity, diversity posture, interconnection footprint, and per-site connectivity readiness — so leadership can see where the backbone constrains growth.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Engage substantively in technical discussions with network engineering and architecture teams — challenge assumptions on route design, capacity planning, and turn-up sequencing, and contribute to problem-solving rather than only reporting status\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Build and continuously improve the systems that make this function scalable: intake workflows, tracking templates, milestone frameworks, and reporting cadences that hold up as the program portfolio grows across domestic and international markets.\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Minimum Within the GFO, the SaaS Technical Support Engineering team supports CoreWeave Forge, the platform ML engineers and researchers use to track experiments, manage models, and build with LLMs. The team works directly with customers to debug training workflows, resolve SDK and API integration issues, and keep their AI development moving. The GFO team works closely with internal and customer engineering teams, so the SaaS TSE team brings insight from the field back to Forge product and engineering and helps shape the CoreWeave product roadmap.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;What You’ll Do:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Support is a deep part of our culture here at CoreWeave. We believe that the best way to build a great product is to listen to real users and follow their lead to shape our priorities and roadmap. In this role, you will work on a diverse set of problems in a fast-moving environment, collaborate cross-functionally with our team to support our users, and help shape our product.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;Your main goal will be to quickly get answers to all user messages relating to CoreWeave’s Forge product. Customers write in with highly technical questions, suggestions, or bug reports, and we need to give them timely responses to fulfill SLAs. Ideally, we\u0026#39;re looking for someone with technical skills who would like to support our customer base. If you\u0026#39;ve found yourself wanting to be more external but still build programming/AI engineering skills, this is the role for you.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;About the role:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Respond to inbound support requests across email, Slack, and community forums, triaging by customer tier and severity and meeting response SLAs\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Own technical escalations end-to-end: investigate using logs, traces, and dashboards (we use Datadog and Grafana), reproduce issues, and write clear, structured escalations that engineering can act on\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Debug issues across the full breadth of our growing Forge product suite — from experiment tracking to agentic AI tooling — across every deployment model, from our cloud to customers\u0026#39; own environments\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Coordinate across engineering, product and other internal teams to drive customer issues to resolution — and keep customers informed with a kind, thoughtful tone throughout\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Recognize incidents, engage on-call engineering through our incident process, and communicate status to affected customers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Be the voice of the customer — advocate for product improvements on their behalf, and spot trends in user messages to improve internal and external documentation\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Deliver clean written handoffs as part of a follow-the-sun support model spanning APAC, North America, and EMEA, with participation in a weekend and holiday on-call rotation\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Mentor teammates on troubleshooting approach and escalation quality, and encourage team building through knowledge sharing and a collaborative, supportive team culture\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Who You Are:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;2+ years of programming experience from an engineering role, CS degree, or substantial personal projects; proficient in Python\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience with logging and monitoring tools such as Datadog or similar logging/APM/tracing platforms\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Working knowledge of web application concepts: REST and GraphQL APIs, authentication flows (SSO, SAML, OAuth/OIDC), browser debugging\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience using developer and AI-assisted tooling such as Claude Code, Codex, and modern debugging tools\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A passion for connecting with real users and enabling them to be power users of the product\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Good organization of assigned requests to oversee timely follow-up for every message\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Work autonomously in a self-directed environment\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Proactively find ways to improve processes and collaborate internally\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;A strong written communicator who can turn a messy investigation into a crisp summary for engineers, and a technical answer into a clear, empathetic reply for customers\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Preferred:\u0026lt;/strong\u0026gt;\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Customer service experience in a technical SaaS environment\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Previous experience in AI development\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience in frontend frameworks\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience with Docker, AWS, GCP, Azure\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;li\u0026gt;Experience with Kubernetes or other cloud infrastructures\u0026lt;/li\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;/ul\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p\u0026gt;\u0026lt;strong\u0026gt;Wondering if you’re a good fit? Reporting to the Director of Treasury Accounting, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the Senior Manager, Treasury Accounting, you will own the day-to-day accounting and operational execution of derivative and hedging activities.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p class=\u0026quot;wnfdntu _1ibi0s3fd _1ibi0s3ce _1ibi0s3eg\u0026quot;\u0026gt;You will partner closely with Treasury, Energy Management, and other cross-functional teams to ensure new transactions are incorporated into accounting and close processes timely and accurately. You will maintain appropriate documentation and supporting information, complete ongoing hedge accounting requirements, and help coordinate recurring activities across Treasury and Treasury Accounting.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;p class=\u0026quot;wnfdntu _1ibi0s3fd _1ibi0s3ce _1ibi0s3eg\u0026quot;\u0026gt;Beyond derivatives, you will help drive the broader operating rhythm of the Treasury Accounting team. This includes coordinating monthly and quarterly deliverables, preparing flux analyses and financial close materials, supporting financial instrument disclosures, and helping build scalable processes as CoreWeave continues to grow. This role requires a strong sense of ownership, sound judgment, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to obtaining information and driving deliverables to completion.\u0026lt;/p\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;h2 class=\u0026quot;wnfdnti _1ibi0s35e _1ibi0s36a\u0026quot;\u0026gt;What You’ll Do\u0026lt;/h2\u0026gt;\n\u0026lt;ul
